full_judgment:
This rule obtained under section 115 C.P.C. is directed against the Order dated 26.6.76 passed by Mr. N. T. Kban, Munsif, Faridpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 191 of 1976. 

 3. The suit was fixed for hearing on 6.4.76. On that date Mr. Md. Sakhawat Hossein, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff submitted an application stating that the sole plaintiff was dead, without stating the date of death. He further stated that as his power to work as the advocate for the plaintiff had ceased, he was unable to take any step in the case. The learned Munsif fixed 16 4.76 as the date of positive bearing of the suit. On the said date no steps were taken by the plaintiff and hence the learned Munsif dismissed the suit for default. 

 4. On 9.6.76 the present petitioners as heirs and successors of the deceased plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 191 of 1976 under Order 9, rule 4 read with section 151 C.P.C. praying for setting aside the order dated 16.4.76 and for restoration of the suit. By his judgment and order dated 26.6 76 the learned Munsif dismissed the Miscellaneous case as not maintainable on the ground that the application was filed more than 30 days after the date of dismissal for default and as such it was barred by limitation. 

 5. Mr. Md. Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case the learned Munsif ought to have taken into consideration that had there been no dismissal for default, the petitioners were still within time in filing an application for substitution of the heirs and successors of the deceased plaintiff. He submits that the learned Munsif should have treated the petitioners' application under Order 9, Rule 4 C.P.C. as basically an application for substitution and should have corrected the erroneous order dated 16.4.76. passed in ignorance of the date of death of the sole plaintiff. Mr. Chaklader submits that this is a fit and proper case where in the interest of justice the learned Munsif, should have exercised his powers under section 151 C.P.C. 

 "3 procedure in case of death of one of several plaintiffs or of sole plaintiff. (1) Where one of two or more plaintiffs dies and the right to sue does not survive to the surviving plaintiff or plaintiffs alone, or a sole plaintiff or sole surviving plaintiff dies and the right to sue survives, the Court, on an application made in that behalf, shall cause the legal representative of the deceased plaintiff to be made a party and shall proceed with the suit. (2) Where within the time limited by law no application is made under sub-rule (1), the suit shall abate so far as the deceased plaintiff is concerned, and on the application of the defendant, the Court may award to him the costs which he may have incurred in defending the suit, to be recovered from the estate of the deceased plaintiff." 

 7. The only order that the learned Munsif could have passed in the present case after being informed of the death of the sole plaintiff was to reword an abatement of the suit. He had no jurisdiction to fix the suit for positive hearing on 16.4.76. When the petitioners filed the present Misc. Case on 9.6:76 they were still within time for substitution under Order 23, Rule 3 C.P.C. Once the fact of the date of death of the deceased plaintiff was known to the learned Munsif, and the date was not controverted, be ought to have realised that the earlier order of dismissal for default was wholly without jurisdiction. He should have retraced his steps under 151 C.P.C. 

 8. I find support for my views in a decision of the Privy Council. In the case of Raja Debi Baksh Singh Vs. Habib Shah XVIII (1913) C.L.J. (PC) 9 the facts were that the plaintiff was dead and it was unknown to the Judge who dismissed the suit for non-appearance of the plaintiff. The deceased plaintiff's son applied within the period of limitation to have his name substituted in place of his deceased father under Order 22, rule 3 C.P C. It was held by the Privy Council that the Rules or Orders of the Code dealing with the case of non-appearance of a suit or were in applicable to a situation when the suits was dead. Upon being pointed out the mistake it was duty of the Court to rectify it. The application of substitution should have been granted and the suit should have been proceeded with. It was also held that quite apart from section 151 C.P.C. the Court possesses an inherent power to rectify the mistake which had been inadvertently committed, but that section could be properly invoked and, apart from points of procedure and otherwise, should be taken advantage of. It was further held that the principle of forfeiture of rights in consequence of a default in procedure by a party to a cause is a principle of punishment in respect of such default, but the punishment of the dead, or this ranking of death under the category of default, does not seem to be very stateable." 

 10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 26 6.76 passed by the learned Munsif in Miscellaneous Case No. 191 of 1976 is set aside. The order dated 16.4.76 passed by the learned Munsif dismissing Title Suit No. 4 of 1974 for default of the plaintiff is also set aside and the said suit is restored to its file and number. The petitioners are substituted as plaintiffs of the said suit as the legal heirs and successors of deceased plaintiff in pursuance of their application dated 9.6.76, subject to any just exception that may be taken by the defendant opposite party at the time of trial. The learned Munsif is directed to proceed with the trial of the said suit.
